arguments.command:
NAME=$(get_timezone | grep 'Timezone Name' | cut -d: -f2 | xargs) &&
OFFSET=$(get_timezone | grep 'Timezone Offset' | cut -d: -f2- | xargs) &&
printf "Timezone: %s (%s)
" "$NAME" "$OFFSET" &&
termy_say -s "Your timezone is $NAME, $OFFSET"
arguments.explanation: Displays the current timezone of the system.

input: alert me when time is up

arguments.command:
termy_question "Enter minutes" MIN &&
termy_question "Enter seconds" SEC &&
m_clean=${MIN#0} &&
s_clean=${SEC#0} &&
m_val=${m_clean:-0} &&
s_val=${s_clean:-0} &&
t=$(( m_val * 60 + s_val )) &&
termy_say -s "Starting timer" &&
while [ $t -gt 0 ]; do
 printf "Time Remaining: %02d:%02d\r" $((t/60)) $((t%60));
 sleep 1;
 t=$((t-1));
done &&
printf "Time's up!" &&
termy_say -s "Time is up" &&
if command -v notify-send >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 notify-send "Countdown Finished" "Your timer is up!";
fi
arguments.explanation: Prompts for minutes and seconds, running a real-time countdown inside the terminal and announcing both the start and finish with termy_say.
arguments.goal: Run an interactive countdown timer with audio alerts

arguments.command:
if command -v cal > /dev/null 2>&1; then OUTPUT_TXT=$(cal); elif command -v ncal > /dev/null 2>&1; then OUTPUT_TXT=$(ncal -b); else OUTPUT_TXT=""; fi && if [ -n "$OUTPUT_TXT" ]; then printf "
📅 \033[1mCurrent Calendar:\033[22m
%s
" "$OUTPUT_TXT" && termy_say "Displaying the current month calendar" > /dev/null 2>&1; else termy_say "Calendar utility is not installed, do you want to install it" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
⛔ Calendar utility not found. Install ncal? y/n: " && read -r ans && case "$ans" in [yY]*) printf "
" && sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y ncal ;; *) printf "
⛔ Operation cancelled.
" ;; esac; fi
arguments.explanation: Displays the current month's calendar using cal or ncal, or prompts to install it if missing.

arguments.command:
termy_say "Please enter the unix timestamp" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
🕐 Unix timestamp: " && read -r ts && if [ -n "$ts" ]; then CONV_DATE=$(date -d @"$ts" 2>/dev/null || date -r "$ts" 2>/dev/null); if [ -n "$CONV_DATE" ]; then printf "
📅 Human Date: \033[1m%s\033[22m
" "$CONV_DATE" && termy_say "The converted date is $CONV_DATE" > /dev/null 2>&1; else printf "
⛔ Invalid timestamp format.
" && termy_say "Invalid timestamp" > /dev/null 2>&1; fi; else printf "
⛔ Timestamp cannot be empty.
" && termy_say "Operation cancelled" > /dev/null 2>&1; fi
arguments.explanation: Converts a Unix timestamp to a human-readable date and handles cross-platform date command syntax.
